messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@orbitai.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Burn-to-Commit alignment + burst planning for OrbitAI Q4 ramp

Team — sharing OrbitAI's updated pipeline and a quick capacity ask. They pushed the pilot to a broader group and expect a 3x query ramp mid-Nov. Sarah attached an updated forecast; key asks are: a reservation uplift starting 2025-11-10 and a predictable burst policy for the first 8 weeks.

Quick context: OrbitAI is a mid-market NLP SaaS customer with a committed Dedicated pool (monthly commit today ~120k token-hours). New pilot converts to production if we can ensure latency <= 80ms p50 and dedicated burst capacity of ~40% above commit for short windows.

Files attached: OrbitAI_Q4_pipeline_forecast_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), burst_profile_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook stub)

Questions / asks:
- Can infra estimate the incremental GPU-hours/slots needed for a 3x sustained increase on their request distribution? (Karthik)
- Finance: what cadence/discount considerations if OrbitAI wants to convert pilot to a Q4-commit with a short-term uplift? (Laura)
- Ops: what guardrails do we need for burst eligibility to protect other reserved customers? (Grace)

Proposed next step: 30-min standup today at 11:30 to align on an actionable commit + burst plan we can share with Sarah. If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burn-to-Commit alignment + burst planning for OrbitAI Q4 ramp

Ben / team — read the forecast. High level thoughts from infra side:

- Baseline calc: a 3x increase across their current qps and token distribution equates to ~1.8x GPU-slot load across the peak windows because of caching and request skew. Rough estimate: +2.5 reserved slots (A100-equivalent) sustained across the 8-week window, plus short-term burst capacity to cover spikes (we should model 4x instantaneous headroom).

- Options:
  * Option A (conservative): reserve +3 slots from 11/10 through 12/31, enable burst policy capped at 50% of slot pool with pre-emption protections.
  * Option B (flexible): reserve +2 slots; allow 8-week burst escrow that can borrow from central burst pool up to 60% but with SLA tiering.

- Risk: if we push too much uncommitted burst to OrbitAI during Black Friday-like traffic from other customers, we will violate p50 latency SLOs for Tier 1 reserved customers. Need finance to sign off on revenue protection (short-term uplift fees or escrow).

I'll bring a baseline numeric model to the 11:30 standup (spreadsheet tab 'InfraCalc' — included in the xlsx). For now, flagging that we need a decision on Option A vs B by EOD today to lock provisioning.

-Karthik

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Date: Tue, 14 Oct 2025 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burn-to-Commit alignment + burst planning for OrbitAI Q4 ramp

Thanks Ben — finance perspective below.

Summary: OrbitAI is at a point where a short-term uplift (one quarter) with a corresponding uplift fee + conversion path into an annual commit makes sense. We should avoid deep discretionary discounts for burst — prefer fixed uplift fee tied to explicit burst usage.

Numbers (back-of-envelope):
- Current commit: ~$28k/month equivalent.
- Proposed short-term uplift (11/10–12/31): +25% commit (~$7k/mo) OR a burst escrow fee of $9k payable upfront to guarantee priority burst access.

Recommendation: present two commercial paths to customer:
  1) Temp commit uplift (+25%) with prorated billing and conversion credit if they convert to annual commit within 30 days after uplift window.
  2) Burst escrow model: upfront fee that pays for reserved capacity we keep idle for the window; usage beyond escrow billed at premium over standard token rates.

I can draft AMAs and pricing language if we agree on Option A vs B.

Laura

Cc: Sarah Lin <sarah@orbitai.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Oct 2025 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Burn-to-Commit alignment + burst planning for OrbitAI Q4 ramp — decision + action items

Thanks all for the fast turn. Quick readout from the standup and the decision we’ll present to OrbitAI: we’ll go with a hybrid path (Option B-heavy) to balance risk and speed-to-market. Key points to confirm with the customer and internal ops: 

1) Capacity decision (Infra): provision +2 reserved slots A100-eq from 2025-11-10 to 2026-01-05. In parallel, grant access to the central burst escrow for up to 60% instantaneous headroom for 8 weeks. Karthik: confirm provisioning window and automated pre-emption policy by EOD today.

2) Commercial (Finance): implement Burst Escrow fee (upfront) at $9k for the window; include conversion credit of 50% of escrow fee if customer converts to annual commit within 30 days after escalation. Laura: please prepare a short SOW and invoice stub.

3) Guardrails (Ops): we will cap burst priority behind Tier 1 reserved customers; if tail latency or p95 for Tier 1 drift >10% we will throttle OrbitAI's burst. Grace: add an alert rule and emergency fallback (auto-fail to reduced-quality model) into the runbook.

4) Communication to customer: Ben — share a one-page summary with the two paths (upli ft vs escrow) and the recommended hybrid; attach the forecast and runbook PDF. I will join the customer call tomorrow 10am PT to confirm wording.

5) Follow-ups: owner list and deadlines below:
  - Karthik: infra calc + provisioning ticket (RESERVE-3912) — due EOD today
  - Laura: draft SOW/invoice and pricing language — due EOD today
  - Ben: customer one-pager + schedule 10am PT call — due by 17:00 today
  - Grace: alert+fallback added to runbook; test plan (smoke) — due tomorrow 12:00 PT

If any objections, flag now. Otherwise I’ll send the customer-facing note and the calendar invite for the 10am slot.

Thanks — Mina
